newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks tumble to new 5-1/2 year low.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks tumble to new 5-1/2 year low.

text.p: Thai stocks took another beating on Tuesday and fell to their lowest closing level in 5-1/2 years as concerns over the sluggish economy and anticipation of weak corporate earnings took their toll, traders said.
The key SET Index, which has been battered by a series of economic problems, dropped 2.55 percent to end at 643.28 points -- its lowest close since November 1, 1991.
The decline was mainly brought on by jitters over the slowing economy's short and medium-term prospects, traders said.
Private economists project Thailand's lagging economy will slow to about five percent this year -- its lowest level in a decade.
Traders say the slow growth expectations and few clear signs of a quick end to the economic downturn sparked sales across the board.
The focus of selling on Tuesday was on the finance sector which was hit by worries of weak loan quality, investment portfolio losses and low broking revenues. The sector dropped 4.54 percent.
Property counters fell 4.46 percent and the communications stocks dropped 5.13 percent.
Thailand was hit by a financial crisis in March when authorities ordered ailing financial institutions to raise capital and set aside more provisions for sub-standard assets.
The moves sparked a run on deposits and caused the stock market to plummet to near five-year lows.
